issues.description: The template Stock.getStockIngredients() returns a List<StockIngredient> (template), while the reference solution's Stock.getStockIngredients() returns a StockIngredient[] array. This is a return-type mismatch that can confuse students about which API to use when inspecting stock contents and may cause difficulties if tests or example code expect one form over the other.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across template and solution. Either change the template method to return StockIngredient[] (and update any uses) or change the solution to return List<StockIngredient>. Update the problem text/examples to reference the chosen form so students know which API to implement against.

issues.description: The problem text instructs students to initialize the SealSaloon attributes (orders and stock) in the constructor, but also explicitly requires that the stock attribute is static (shared across instances) and final. Initializing a static field in an instance constructor is incorrect and contradictory: a static final field should be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer. This contradiction can mislead students about where and how to declare and initialize the shared stock.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the problem statement: state that 'stock' must be declared static final and initialized at the point of declaration or in a static initializer (not in the instance constructor). If the intent was an instance field, remove the requirement that it be static. Update the instructions to consistently describe whether 'stock' is shared (static) or per-instance and show the recommended initialization approach.
